subject: Test statistic values for F-test/ChiSq for adjusting p-value distribution

messages.author: 9c69ed22aa4df507
messages.subject: Test statistic values for F-test/ChiSq for adjusting p-value distribution
parts:
Hi,

Is it possible to somehow extract the test statistic values of the F-test or ChiSq tests after calculateMethDiff? Now the output is only with p and q values and the methylation difference. As my p-value distributions are mostly not uniform (regardless of the analysis package used to get it) I would like to be able to compare the different p-value adjustment strategies between different analysis packages. I know methylKit uses SLIM, but I would also like to try fdrtool which uses a different way of adjusting for the skew in the uniform null model expectation, but for fdrtool I would need the original test statistic values to do the adjustment.

In general I would also be interested to hear if any other readers of this discussion group have looked in detail to their p-value distributions, and if they have tried other ways than SLIM to adjust them? Or if you have compared different null model distribution adjustment methods?

Thanks!
Heidi

parts:
it is not possible to extract the test statistic values. For most, P-value correction methods you just need a vector of P-values. Have you tried the qvalue from qvalue package? That is usually more robust than SLIM

Best,
Altuna

messages.author: 9c69ed22aa4df507
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Test statistic values for F-test/ChiSq for adjusting p-value distribution
parts:
I have tried qvalue but compared to SLIM it leaves no significant hits behind (and this is a common feature regardless of the analysis package I've used so far).

I believe the lack of significance after p-value correction is due to the consistent right-hand skewed p-value distribution and therefore I have doubts whether or not I can actually trust the results I get. I also tried fdrtool in which you can use the test statistic values to acquire an empirical null distribution and then identify the q-value based on that; this leaves me with significant hits and p-value distribution that is uniform. If I run fdrtool with p-values instead it assumes normal null distribution (as does qvalue as I understood) and nothing remains significant. To my understanding the SLIM method is something of in between empirical and normal null expectation as it tries to fit several linears to the null distribution obtained from the data and by that obtain a correction factor used to get the q-values.

How big violations from normally distributed null model can SLIM handle in your opinion? All the examples of p-value distributions in Wang et al 2011 (the SLIM paper) are not as skewed as mine. I attached an example from methylKit but with I've seen even more even right-hand skewed distributions with other packages.

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Test statistic values for F-test/ChiSq for adjusting p-value distribution
parts:
Maybe SLIM can handle this if you fiddle with its parameters, we are just using the defaults. But the main problem is probably that the peak on the right tail screws up the estimation of pi0. If you also look at the function pi0est function in qvalue package you may be able to estimate pi0 only from portion of the histogram that looks like a uniform distribution by playing with lambda argument. I have never done this but looking at the qvalue documentation this seems possible.

Best,
Altuna
